title.en: Reproduction in plants, animals and humans

text.en: A potato sprouts from an eye, a hen lays eggs and a mother gives birth. Different methods, one purpose: life continues.

Reproduction is the process by which organisms produce new individuals of their own kind.
Asexual reproduction involves one parent and gives offspring identical to it. Examples are binary fission, budding, fragmentation and vegetative propagation.
Sexual reproduction involves two parents and the fusion of gametes, so offspring show variation.
In flowers, pollination is the transfer of pollen from anther to stigma. It can be self or cross pollination, by wind, water, insects or animals.
After fertilisation the ovule becomes a seed and the ovary becomes a fruit.
In animals sexual reproduction involves fertilisation, which may be external, as in frogs, or internal, as in humans.
In humans the male gamete is the sperm and the female gamete is the egg. The fertilised egg is a zygote that develops in the uterus.
Sexual reproduction increases variation, which helps species survive changes in the environment.

problem.en: Why do children of the same parents look different from each other?

text.en: Each child receives a different mix of genes from the two parents.
Fertilisation combines sperm and egg randomly.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking pollination and fertilisation are the same

points.en: Asexual reproduction needs one parent; sexual needs two.
Pollination is the transfer of pollen; fertilisation is the fusion of gametes.
The zygote develops into an embryo.
